# Verdict: ACCEPT-WITH-RESERVATIONS ## Findings **Pre-commitment Predictions**: Before reading the code, I predicted: (1) redundant ARIA roles on native elements, (2) unassociated tabular data in list items, (3) potential `aria-atomic` noise if parent updates frequently, (4) strong focus persistence due to persistent button, (5) borderline contrast on error state. Actual findings align with predictions 1, 2, and 4. Prediction 3 is mitigated by the component's design (full replacement per update). Prediction 5 passes but lacks safety margin. **Critical Findings**: None. The component implements core accessibility patterns correctly and avoids blocking barriers for any user group. **Major Findings**: 1. **List items lack programmatic association between payee and amount.** - **Evidence**: `src/components/AccountActivityPanel.tsx:38-40` renders `{t.payee}` and `{t.amount}` as independent siblings inside `
  • `. - **User Group Impacted**: Screen reader users. AT will announce payee and amount as four separate, unlinked items rather than a single transaction record. - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (programmatic association of related information); WAI-ARIA APG Principle: Native HTML first / Semantic structure must match user intent. - **Fix**: Add `aria-label` to each `
  • ` combining both values, e.g., `
  • `, or convert to a semantic `` with `
    ` headers if the data is tabular in nature. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: Screen reader users lose the relationship between payee and amount, forcing them to mentally reconstruct transaction records from disjointed announcements. ``` ### A11y Evidence Finding finding_id: list-item-semantic-gap fingerprint: a7f3c9d2e1b4 source: src/components/AccountActivityPanel.tsx:38-40 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; WAI-ARIA APG Native HTML First section_508_fpc_context: Not in scope (WCAG 2.2 AA target) severity: MAJOR perspective_alarms: screen reader=HIGH, keyboard=LOW, low vision=LOW, cognitive=LOW evidence:
  • {t.payee} {t.amount}
    • reproduction_steps: Render component with status='ready' and transactions=[{id:1, payee:'Acme', amount:'$50.00'}]. Navigate to list item via screen reader. expected_behavior: Screen reader announces a single transaction record with payee and amount programmatically associated. actual_behavior: Screen reader announces four independent items: "Payee Acme Amount $50.00" without relationship context. trend: new ``` **Minor Findings**: 1. **Redundant `role="list"` on native `
      `** - **Evidence**: `src/components/AccountActivityPanel.tsx:35` `
        ` - **User Group Impacted**: All AT users (minor noise/confusion) - **WCAG/APG Citation**: WAI-ARIA APG Principle: Native HTML first. Do not use ARIA roles when equivalent semantics are available in HTML. - **Fix**: Remove `role="list"`. The native `
          ` already conveys list semantics to all assistive technologies. - **Confidence**: HIGH **Enhancements**: 1. **Error color contrast lacks safety margin** - **Evidence**: `src/components/AccountActivityPanel.css:4` `.panel-error { color: #b42318; }` on white background yields ~4.63:1. Passes AA (4.5:1) but fails AAA (7:1). - **Fix**: Darken to `#991b15` or `#8b1a10` for a comfortable safety margin against device calibration variations. WCAG 1.4.3. 2. **List lacks explicit heading/label context** - **Evidence**: The `
            ` is implicitly part of the section labeled by `activity-heading`, but screen readers won't explicitly announce "Transactions list" before reading items. - **Fix**: Add `aria-label="Transaction list"` to the `
              ` or ensure the parent section heading clearly scopes the list context. **What's Missing**: - **Programmatic row association in list**: Payee and amount are visually paired but programmatically independent. Screen readers cannot infer the relationship without `aria-label` or table semantics. - **Explicit list labeling**: While scoped to the section, adding `aria-label` to the `
                ` improves landmark/list context for AT users navigating by region. **Multi-Perspective Notes**: | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |-------------|-------------|----------------| | Screen reader | HIGH | Unassociated payee/amount spans; redundant role on list | | Keyboard-only | LOW | Persistent button, logical tab order, visible focus indicator | | Low vision | LOW | Focus meets 3:1+ contrast; `prefers-reduced-motion` handled; flex reflow acceptable | | Cognitive | LOW | Clear state labels; error message names recovery action; no timeouts | | Vestibular & motion | LOW | Spinner animation suppressed via media query | | Auditory access | LOW | No audio elements present | | Environmental contrast | MEDIUM | Error color passes AA but lacks AAA margin; focus indicator meets threshold | **Verdict Justification**: The component demonstrates excellent accessibility design choices: persistent DOM regions prevent focus destruction during state changes, `role="status"` and `role="alert"` are correctly scoped to their urgency levels, `aria-atomic="true"` appropriately handles full content replacement, and the spinner is properly hidden from AT. The primary reservation is the semantic gap in the transaction list (MAJOR finding), which breaks programmatic association for screen reader users. Removing the redundant `role="list"` and associating payee/amount values will resolve this. With these two targeted fixes, the design is production-ready. **Open Questions (unscored)**: 1. Does the parent component update the `status` region via polling or rapid state changes? If so, `aria-atomic="true"` may cause jarring full-region re-announcements. Consider debouncing updates or using `aria-relevant="additions text"` if partial updates become necessary. 2. Is the transaction data truly list-based or tabular? If users frequently compare amounts across rows, a `` with `
                ` headers would be semantically superior to a flexbox list. 3. Does the parent disable `onRetry` during in-flight requests? The component comments note this is the parent's responsibility, but verifying that disabled state uses `disabled=""` (not just CSS opacity) ensures AT correctly reads it as inert.
